chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Draft notice and induction at Camp Upton
summary: He worked fifteen days after the March notice, then reported to Whitehall Street and Camp Upton.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Okay, all right, we'll get to that later. In 1943 most of your men are in the service and then you get a letter from President Roosevelt that you were drafted. Tell me about that, when you opened that mailbox in ....

In March. It was a big envelope and I was acquainted with the envelope already because Pin Madera received one, you know, so I said to myself, well, they got me. They give me fifteen days, so I worked the fifteen days because I need the money for my family; so that particular morning, Sunday morning or Monday morning, I went to Whitehall and from Whitehall we went to Camp Upton in the White area. It was a new experience altogether, I got there about six o'clock in the morning. It was drizzling, you know, it was in April and it was a very interesting experience.
